cases.statement: One person (Table 2 #40), listed in both copies of the same preprint; homozygous for c.644_647delTGGG. No individual clinical description.

people.label: Table 2 #40
people.key_phenotypes: not reported individually (cohort-level data only) (same preprint text as 37503297)

phenotype_specificity.statement: Only cohort-level phenotype data; the cohort was enrolled after genetic confirmation of SSADHD. No statement about testing of other genes.

quotes.quote: Movement disorders were present in 32 (55%) subjects: 30 (52%) had ataxia, 14 (24%) had dyskinesia, and 9 (15%) had dystonia.
After being genetically confirmed with SSADHD, subjects enrolled in the natural history study undergo a series of clinical and laboratory assessments biennially.

in_trans.statement: Homozygous call in Table 2. Parental testing is not reported, and this row carries no consanguinity asterisk (Table 2 marks consanguinity with *). A large deletion on the second allele was not addressed in the paper.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Four-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift (predicted p.(Val215GlyfsTer12)) in exon 4, in the region the paper assigns to the NAD+ binding domain. The paper describes the disease as autosomal recessive and states that biallelic premature stops give no functional protein.

quotes.quote: Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) (OMIM #271980) is a rare (prevalent in ~ 1/460,000^1) inherited metabolic disorder caused by autosomal recessive inheritance of ALDH5A1 sequence variants^2.
If the genetic variant (insertion or deletion) results in a premature stop codon on both alleles, a functional SSADH protein would not be synthesized.

computational_predictions.statement: No variant-level score is given for this frameshift. The authors' model assigns this genotype to "Truncated/inactive" with effect "No protein".

authors_classification.statement: Authors list c.644_647delTGGG among eight previously unreported variants and make a blanket statement covering all 32 cohort variants.

quotes.quote: eight of which were previously unreported (c.104_127 del, c.127delC, c.870 + 1G > T, 6p22.3 deletion, c.644_647delTGGG, c.1558G > C, c.755G > A, and c.1388del) (Table 1)
This study’s findings determined that the 32 allelic variants (eight of which are novel), present in 41 unique allelic combinations (Table 1) in 58 SSADHD participants, were pathogenic.

concerns: PMIDs 37503297 and 37962671 carry the same Research Square preprint text (DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-3111263/v1); 37962671 states a version was later published in Human Genetics. The two rows are one person counted once (same identity), not independent observations.

The person appears only as a numbered row in a genotype table of a natural-history cohort; there is no individual case description, sex, age or phenotype for this row. The cohort is 58 individuals from 50 families, so some rows are relatives, but the paper does not say which.
Homozygosity is a table label only; parents were not reported as tested, so a deletion of the other allele or uniparental disomy cannot be excluded from the paper.
Protein notation differs in style only: the paper writes V215GfsX11, the batch prediction is p.(Val215GlyfsTer12); the batch marks the protein check as agreeing.
No transcript is stated in this paper.
notes_for_panel: Evidence is limited to a genotype-table row in a cohort preprint; the blanket author statement covers all 32 cohort variants.
